correctness.rationale: For odd \(q\) the map \(t\mapsto(t,t^{-1})\) has unique unordered representations for every nonzero two-point sum: the roots of \(Z^2-xZ+x/y\) reconstruct the pair. Zero sums are exactly antipodal pairs. Orthogonality yields the factor \(q^2/(q-1)^4\); an exact pair-sum expansion yields \(\mathcal Q=2M^2-\sum_i(A_i^2+|B_i|^2/2)+|B|^2\). Completing squares gives the three-term identity; \(|B|\le M\) and positive coefficients establish nonnegativity and exact equality. This proof works for all odd prime powers. A separate standard-library checker executed 225 coefficient cases and 12,825 direct Fourier sums over \(q\in\{3,5,7,9,11\}\).

value.rationale: Finite-field quadratic-curve extension is a canonical harmonic-analysis question. The exact finite-q optimal constant (not mere asymptotic boundedness), complete complex equality manifold for every odd prime power, and a three-term quantitative deficit identity that controls mass balance and antipodal phase coherence are structural information with a plausible role in stable extension and near-extremizer problems. Not an arbitrary chosen index or routine substitution: the exceptional zero-sum fiber creates a different extremizer geometry from the parabola and anisotropic spheres.
